authority.rule: Only the producer that writes an analysis artifact may bind that exact artifact content to the validated Atlas payload it consumed.
authority.content_binding: The receipt artifact_sha256 must match the canonical JSON hash of the evidence payload consumed by proof.
authority.dependency_rule: Every declared lineage dependency must have a COMPLETE content-matching receipt for the same Atlas snapshot; otherwise the new receipt is BLOCKED.

ts_diagnostics.syntax_root_identity_rule: Compare the collector's recorded project root with the Atlas project's recorded absolute lexical path identity, without resolving either path against the live target filesystem during receipt creation. Reject missing, relative, traversal-bearing or aliased roots even if a later live resolution reaches the same directory. This binds the recorded root name and checked syntax text only; it does not establish physical link stability, config-content identity or semantic type safety.
ts_diagnostics.frontier_syntax_claim_rule: A COMPLETE checked-syntax receipt permits only a separate checked-file syntax diagnostic finding. Do not label it a type-contract failure or raise the score, confidence or evidence kind of co-located React type, RSC, security or hydration heuristics. File co-location does not establish causal correlation. Semantic diagnostics remain unavailable while semantic lineage is BLOCKED; future cross-finding correlation requires risk-specific, span-level evidence.
ts_diagnostics.root_config_selection_rule: Syntax and semantic collector modes select the same contract-owned simple JSON/JSONC filename at each validated project root. The collector must not silently fall back when this policy is unavailable. The semantic snapshot binder rejects another reported config path even when that path has an observed Atlas-bound read. Syntax source-text lineage does not bind config content. This binds SAGE's declared root-config selection, not the target's native config choice, parsed extends closure, compiler options, project references or native-project semantics.

atlas_auxiliary_inputs.rule: Capture bounded UTF-8 input identities from the existing owned Atlas walk, not a second scan. Preserve raw-byte and TypeScript host-text identities without contents. The same resolved path used for the bounded auxiliary read also records whether its exact literal file path was canonical; an internal file link is false. Missing, unreadable, oversized, non-UTF-8, excluded or surgical-only inputs remain unavailable. The canonicality bit is enumeration-time auxiliary evidence only, not source-file or atomic link authority. Inventory absence never proves a negative module-resolution result.

atlas_resolution_inputs.rule: Capture complete immediate directory names before pruning during the existing Atlas walk. Only a missing literal name in a captured canonical directory can establish snapshot-relative absence. An unvisited, failed, aliased, omitted or surgical directory stays unknown. Preserve excluded names as present boundaries; do not traverse them. Reject internally inconsistent source/directory presence. Uncaptured Windows short-name aliases, reserved/trailing-dot namespaces and Unicode equivalence stay unknown rather than inheriting literal-name absence. This is directory enumeration evidence, not atomic filesystem stability, compiler-library authority or semantic completeness.

compiler_library_inputs.rule: For explicit semantic collection only, the invoking producer captures the installed TypeScript declaration identities before launching Node. Resolve ownership through third_party_distribution_contract, not child-reported paths. Reconcile actual positive library reads with that invocation-bound inventory. Reject unavailable, aliased, changed, malformed and over-budget input; never reopen child-selected paths. An installed entry hash is not loaded-code attestation, atomic filesystem stability, Atlas authority, negative lookup evidence or native-project equivalence. Syntax-only collection does not perform this capture.

semantic_context.recursive_directory_boundary_rule: Both syntax and semantic config parsing guard each actual recursive directory enumeration before TypeScript reads its entries. Reuse the existing workspace boundary in the scoped synchronous filesystem adapter; filtering returned files is not confinement. Preserve accepted in-boundary links and compiler glob semantics without an additional walk. Refused or failed recursive enumeration makes config coverage incomplete and cannot authorize a complete syntax manifest; configured roots dropped by boundary filtering also remain incomplete. Record semantic host failures through the existing observation budget. Restore filesystem wrappers in finally. The check is not atomic confinement against concurrent link replacement, recursive-input snapshot reconciliation or native-project proof.
semantic_context.compiler_working_directory_rule: Each project's config and compiler hosts use that project's validated root as getCurrentDirectory, and config parsing receives its actual tsconfig path. Do not chdir the shared Node process or use the installation directory as an implicit target type root. Record compiler-host and process working directories separately. This fixes automatic type-discovery context without enabling target plugins, restoring removed bounded options, traversing additional Atlas scope or claiming native-project equivalence. Recursive glob snapshot binding remains separate.
semantic_context.host_io_failure_rule: In the isolated synchronous semantic collector, observe the filesystem calls actually made by TypeScript, including swallowed read/stat/list/realpath errors and statSync missing-entry returns. Install before compiler loading and restore in finally; do not reread or rescan. Preserve actual host results with bounded operation, code and count metadata, never raw messages or error paths. Only ENOENT for an already-missing direct file/directory existence or read query is expected absence. Failure after a present boundary check, failed enumeration and realpath fallback remain unavailable. This does not prove atomic path stability, list/glob or link-target binding, or native-project equivalence.
semantic_context.positive_lookup_rule: Match exact literal file-existence results backed by captured content, directory-existence results backed by canonical owned-walk records, and returned canonical-directory paths. A file realpath result matches only when its observed result equals the literal path, captured ancestors are canonical, and either a content-bearing auxiliary file has exact literal-path canonicality from its owned read or an Atlas source file has a true canonical-file bit and valid captured source text identity. Atlas computes the source bit during the existing ownership resolution, refreshes it on normal, staged and cached full walks, and omits new authority in surgical scans. Legacy rows lacking the bit, aliases and excluded dependencies remain unresolved. Match getDirectories only when every immediate entry has captured file content or its own canonical directory record, query arguments are empty, and exact sorted ASCII basenames match the observed count and digest. Reject unknown, duplicate, case-ambiguous, aliased, failed or filtered entries; absence of a child record is not proof of a file. Require captured ancestors and reject contradictory file/directory images. Reuse one projection per queried directory without live I/O. Recursive inputs follow recursive_directory_input_rule. Matching inputs does not independently replay compiler outputs or prove atomic filesystem stability, link-target persistence or native-project equivalence.
semantic_context.positive_workspace_read_rule: Compare every observed positive workspace readFile host text with captured Atlas source identity using the central SHA-256 or legacy MD5 text-hash policy, or with an owned auxiliary host-text SHA-256 identity, without reopening the target. Missing, malformed, out-of-scope, changed or BOM-normalized source text remains unbound; a complete observation list with no positive workspace read is not proof. Compiler-library reads retain their separate pre-invocation owner. This is partial input correspondence only: physical file/link identity, compiler options, references, atomic stability and semantic lineage/scoring remain unresolved.
semantic_context.reported_root_config_read_rule: The semantic collector's reported tsconfig path must match the contract-selected root filename and have exactly one successful config-stage readFile observation, reconciled with the owned Atlas auxiliary host-text identity. A source or inherited-config read cannot substitute for the root config. The existing positive workspace-read check separately reconciles observed extends and other config inputs. This proves SAGE's selected root read/content correspondence, not that the target's native build selects the same config, complete transitive extends coverage, parsed compiler options, project-reference semantics, atomic filesystem stability or semantic scoring.
semantic_context.configured_roots_digest_rule: When the collector reports equal configured and selected root counts, both digests must be valid and equal; the selected digest is separately reconciled with the checked-source manifest. If selection is partial, the configured-list digest remains producer observation only. This catches an internal contradiction without independently deriving tsconfig roots, compiler options, references or full Program authority, and cannot enable semantic scoring.
semantic_context.empty_project_references_digest_rule: A reported zero project-reference count must carry the canonical SHA-256 digest of an empty JSON array. A nonzero count remains explicitly unloaded; its digest cannot be independently reconstructed from the count. This is a producer-field contradiction check only, not Atlas-bound reference discovery, native project equivalence or semantic-scoring authority.
semantic_context.semantic_profile_negative_rule: The collector's requested-options digest, effective options, sorted overridden option names and project-reference count/digest are negative evidence only. Missing or malformed profile/reference observations are unavailable; any overridden option or unloaded project reference is an explicit lineage blocker. Cross-check selected root count and normalized absolute-path digest against the checked-source manifest, and reject a configured count below the selected count; this is producer-field consistency only, not independent config or Atlas authority. A self-reported empty override list or zero references is not independent Atlas binding or native-project equivalence. The installed native compiler and bounded collector must be compared on a source-grounded alias fixture: a bounded TS2307 absent from the native result is not a target-repository defect and cannot enter Merge scoring.
semantic_context.semantic_program_project_source_rule: From the existing TypeScript Program SourceFiles, prioritize project-local non-declaration dependencies after emitted diagnostic files and selected roots, ahead of compiler libraries, under the existing manifest file budget. Record only a bounded list of manifest-covered project-source names and the observed total. Compare each recorded source text identity to the owning Atlas project without reopening target files; missing, stale, malformed or budget-omitted input remains explicit. This is lexical project-local SourceFile correspondence, not independent proof of the reported total, full Program inputs, physical link stability, compiler options, excluded dependencies, native-project equivalence or semantic Merge scoring.
semantic_context.semantic_program_project_declaration_rul: Within the same bounded Program manifest, prioritize lexically project-local declaration SourceFiles after diagnostic files, selected roots and project-local non-declaration dependencies, before compiler libraries. Compare each recorded declaration SourceFile text SHA-256 with the owning Atlas auxiliary host-text SHA-256; require the existing owned auxiliary inventory and exact normalized relative path. Missing, stale, malformed and budget-omitted declaration inputs remain explicit. No extra read or walk is permitted. This is text correspondence only; observed declaration counts, declarations outside the project, complete Program inputs, physical links, native compiler context and semantic Merge scoring remain unbound.
semantic_context.semantic_program_workspace_external_rule: For Program SourceFiles lexically inside the configured workspace but outside the current project, record a bounded absolute path and declaration bit under the same existing manifest budget, after project-local files and before compiler libraries. Compare recorded text only against a unique exact-content owner entry in the canonical Atlas project map: ordinary source uses its Atlas source hash, declaration uses the owner's captured auxiliary host-text hash. Missing or duplicate owners, stale text, malformed paths and budget omission remain explicit. A matching entry establishes cross-project text correspondence, not path-derived ownership, current execution of preserved-only projects, complete Program membership, physical/link identity, native compiler context, out-of-workspace library authority or semantic Merge scoring. Do not reread targets, traverse directories or promote a self-reported zero count.
semantic_context.semantic_program_installed_library_rule: Record out-of-workspace Program SourceFiles under the existing bounded checked-source manifest, after project-local and workspace-internal inputs. The producer owner compares each recorded installed TypeScript declaration SourceFile text with its separately held pre-invocation library inventory and requires that the same library was observed as a positive matched compiler-host read. Non-library external paths, stale text, missing or duplicate manifest entries, malformed paths and budget omission block this partial owner reconciliation. This establishes only bounded installed-library Program text correspondence, not full Program membership, loaded compiler-code attestation, atomic installation or link stability, independent configured-root/options/references authority, native-project equivalence or semantic lineage/Merge scoring. Never reopen a collector-selected path.
semantic_context.recursive_directory_input_rule: For explicit semantic readDirectory calls, observe successful readdirSync and realpath calls inside the existing scoped filesystem adapter, excluding boundary-check probes. Store only paths, sorted file/directory name counts and digests, unsupported-entry counts and call coverage. Use one shared max_observations budget for host rows and recursive rows across all queries, and reuse atlas_resolution_inputs max_entries/max_name_bytes as aggregate per-project capture budgets. Do not truncate compiler diagnostics when evidence is omitted. Reconcile complete trace inputs against canonical owned Atlas directories, every immediate captured file/directory kind and exact resolved-directory identity; preserve equal enumeration/realpath coverage and strict call counts. Omitted, failed, malformed, aliased, link-followed, untyped, excluded or unsupported inputs remain unbound. Cache projections and never reopen targets, walk again, reproduce glob matching or change Atlas capture scope. Old result-only rows have no recursive input authority. This is input correspondence under the recorded compiler/query context, not independent output replay, full semantic lineage, atomic stability or native-project equivalence.
semantic_context.rule: Capture actual host reads, negative resolution probes, config inheritance, compiler identity and effective options without reopening source contents. Record the access decision used by each call: in-boundary missing paths, outside-boundary refusals, unavailable reads and present inputs are distinct. Compiler-library reads carry their toolchain scope and actual returned-text identity; the installed entry identity is observed before analysis, not asserted as a trusted Atlas toolchain snapshot. Complete observation is not Atlas binding or native-project type proof; omitted context, filtered directory entries and bounded-profile differences remain explicit.

ts_diagnostics.claim_boundary: Exact checked syntax source and bounded semantic diagnostic/selected-root/project-local, unique-Atlas cross-project and separately inventoried installed-library Program text correspondence only. Truncation, missing source identity, incomplete Program inputs, semantic compiler/configuration context and empty checked scope do not establish project-wide type safety.
